questions.question: ‘Kabuli Bagh Mosque’ of Panipat was constructed by which Mughal ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kabuli Bagh Mosque was constructed by Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• It was built in 1527 AD after Babur's victory over Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat.
 
• The mosque is located in Panipat, Haryana, and serves as a significant historical and architectural landmark.
 
• It is named 'Kabuli Bagh' after Babur's wife Kabuli Begum, commemorating his victory.
 
• The mosque represents the early Mughal architecture style, combining Persian and Indian elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**

 
 
• Fought on April 21, 1526, between the forces of Babur and Ibrahim Lodhi.
 
• Marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Babur's use of field artillery was a decisive factor in his victory.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Known for its large-scale use of marble, intricate carvings, and garden layouts.
 
• Famous structures include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Babur:**
 
 
• Full name: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur.
 
• Descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.
 
• Authored his autobiography, Baburnama, which provides a detailed account of his life.
 
 
 
• **Panipat:**
 
 
• A historical city in Haryana, known for three pivotal battles that shaped Indian history.
 
• Besides the First Battle, the Second Battle (1556) and the Third Battle (1761) were also fought here.

questions.question: Right to Education has been given in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 21A** of the Indian Constitution mandates the provision of free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This Article was inserted by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• The Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 operationalizes the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• The RTE Act came into effect on **April 1, 2010**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**

 
 
• This amendment also added Article 45 and Article 51A(k) to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 45 directs the state to provide early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years.
 
• Article 51A(k) mandates parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**
 
 
• The RTE Act aims at providing primary education to all children in the age group of 6-14 years.
 
• It mandates 25% reservation for disadvantaged sections of the society where disadvantaged groups include SCs, STs, socially and educationally backward classes and differently-abled children.
 
• The Act requires all private schools to reserve 25% of their seats for children from these disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• These are a set of rights that are recognized by the Supreme Court as requiring a high degree of protection from government encroachment.
 
• They are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following regarding the trophic levels is INCORRECT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Omnivores-Fungus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Omnivores are organisms that consume both plants and animals as their primary food sources.
 
• Fungi are not classified as omnivores; they are primarily decomposers that break down organic matter.
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, play a crucial role in nutrient cycling by breaking down dead organisms.
 
• Herbivores, also known as primary consumers, feed exclusively on plant material.
 
• Carnivores, which can be secondary or tertiary consumers, feed on other animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels:**

 
 
• The position an organism occupies in a food chain, which includes primary producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and decomposers.
 
• Primary producers, like plants, convert solar energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Food Chain:**
 
 
• A linear sequence of organisms where each is fed upon by the next member in the chain.
 
 
 
• **Food Web:**
 
 
• A complex network of interconnected food chains in an ecosystem, demonstrating how different organisms are interdependent.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Organisms like bacteria and fungi that break down dead matter, returning essential nutrients to the ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transfer:**
 
 
• In ecosystems, energy flows from primary producers through various consumer levels, with significant energy loss at each trophic level due to metabolic processes.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Solids have the highest density compared to liquids, gases, and plasma because their particles are packed closely together in a fixed structure.
 
• The density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume. Solids generally exhibit the highest mass per unit volume among the states of matter.
 
• Examples of high-density solids include metals such as iron, gold, and lead, which have densities significantly higher than liquids and gases.
 
• Solids retain a fixed shape and volume, contributing to their higher density, whereas liquids and gases conform to the shape of their containers and have lower densities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density**

 
 
• Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.
 
• The formula for density is: Density = Mass / Volume.
 
 
 
• **States of Matter**
 
 
• There are four fundamental states of matter: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
 
• Each state has distinct physical properties, such as shape, volume, and particle arrangement.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Densities**
 
 
• Solids typically have the highest densities, followed by liquids, gases, and then plasma.
 
• Water has a density of approximately 1 g/cm³ at standard temperature and pressure, while air has a density of about 0.0012 g/cm³.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma is a high-energy state of matter where electrons are stripped from atoms, creating a mixture of positively charged ions and free electrons.
 
• Plasma densities are typically lower than those of solids, liquids, and gases under terrestrial conditions.

questions.question: Which of the below mentioned elements occurs when the government's revenue expenditure is more than its revenue receipts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Revenue Deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Deficit** occurs when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts.
 
• It indicates the government is not earning sufficient revenue to cover its routine expenses.
 
• Revenue Deficit needs to be managed to avoid excessive borrowing for recurring expenditures.
 
• It is a critical indicator of the financial health of the government and reflects the sustainability of its fiscal policy.
 
• High revenue deficits over time can lead to higher debt levels and interest payments, affecting the overall economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**

 
 
• It measures the total borrowing requirements of the government.
 
• Fiscal Deficit is the difference between total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• A high fiscal deficit can lead to inflation and higher interest rates in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Deficit:**
 
 
• It is a broad term that encompasses both revenue deficit and fiscal deficit.
 
• Budgetary Deficit indicates the overall shortfall in the government's budget.
 
 
 
• **Capital Deficit:**
 
 
• It refers to the shortfall in the capital receipts compared to the capital expenditures.
 
• Capital Deficit typically deals with long-term investments and infrastructure spending.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**
 
 
• These are the funds received by the government from various sources like taxes, duties, and fees.
 
• Revenue Receipts do not create any liabilities or reduce any assets of the government.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Expenditure:**
 
 
• It includes all expenses incurred for the normal functioning of government departments and various services.
 
• Revenue Expenditure does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities.

questions.question: Senani', 'Kulapa' and 'Gramani' are some of the functionaries mentioned primarily in which Veda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rigveda is one of the oldest and most important texts in the Vedic literature.
 
• It is primarily a collection of hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• The Rigveda mentions various functionaries such as 'Senani' (military commander), 'Kulapa' (head of a family or clan), and 'Gramani' (village headman).
 
• These roles were crucial in the social and administrative organization during the Vedic period.
 
• The Rigveda is written in early Vedic Sanskrit and consists of 1,028 hymns in 10 books (Mandalas).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Senani:** The term 'Senani' refers to a military commander responsible for leading and organizing troops during warfare in the Vedic period.
 
• **Kulapa:** 'Kulapa' denotes the head of a family or a clan, playing a significant role in maintaining family or clan order and traditions.
 
• **Gramani:** 'Gramani' was the term used for a village headman, overseeing village administration and local governance.
 
• **Vedic Literature:** The Vedic texts are divided into four main categories: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda, each serving different purposes in the Vedic rituals and knowledge system.
 
• **Vedic Society:** The society during the Vedic period was organized into various roles and responsibilities, with a clear hierarchy and division of labor, which is reflected in the functionaries mentioned in the texts.

questions.question: Trishulganga is a stream of the river:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Trishulganga is a stream of the river **Gandak**, which is also known as the Narayani in Nepal.
 
• The Gandak River is a significant river in Nepal and India, originating from the Himalayas in Nepal.
 
• The river flows through the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh before merging with the Ganges River.
 
• The Gandak River is known for its extensive river system and is a vital source of irrigation and water supply in the regions it traverses.
 
• Trishulganga is one of the many tributaries that contribute to the Gandak River's flow and volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandak River System**

 
 
• The Gandak River has two main tributaries: the Kali Gandaki and Trishuli rivers, which originate in the high Himalayas.
 
• The Kali Gandaki is one of the major rivers in Nepal, known for its deep gorges and rich biodiversity.
 
• The Trishuli River is a famous river in Nepal, popular for rafting and other adventure sports.
 
• The combined flow of these tributaries forms the Gandak River, which plays a crucial role in the ecology and economy of the regions it flows through.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation and Agriculture**
 
 
• The Gandak River basin is one of the most fertile regions in the Indian subcontinent, supporting extensive agricultural activities.
 
• The river provides irrigation to millions of hectares of farmland in both Nepal and India.
 
• Crops like rice, wheat, sugarcane, and pulses are majorly cultivated in the Gandak basin.
 
• The Gandak Canal system is one of the oldest and largest irrigation systems in India, benefiting farmers in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Ecological Importance**
 
 
• The Gandak River supports a diverse range of flora and fauna, including several endangered species.
 
• The river's ecosystem provides habitat to aquatic species like the Gangetic dolphin and various species of fish.
 
• The riverbanks and floodplains are home to numerous bird species, making it an important area for bird conservation.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve the ecological balance of the river through various environmental initiatives.

questions.question: The first National Games, on the line of Olympics, were held in _____
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first National Games of India, modeled on the Olympics, were held in 1924 in New Delhi.
 
• The event was originally known as the Indian Olympic Games.
 
• The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was responsible for organizing these games.
 
• New Delhi was chosen as the venue due to its infrastructure and capacity to host large-scale events.
 
• The National Games have since evolved and are held regularly across various states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**

 
 
• Founded in 1927, the IOA is the governing body for the Olympic movement and Commonwealth Games in India.
 
• It is responsible for selecting athletes to represent India at the Olympic Games, Asian Games, and other international athletic meets.
 
• The IOA also promotes and develops sports in India through national federations.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the National Games**
 
 
• The National Games are held every two years, rotating among different states.
 
• They aim to identify sporting talent and provide a platform for athletes to compete at a national level.
 
• Modern editions of the National Games include a wide range of sports, reflecting the diversity of Indian sports.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the National Games**
 
 
• The games play a crucial role in promoting sports culture and encouraging youth participation in sports.
 
• They help in the development of sports infrastructure in various states.
 
• The National Games serve as a preparatory ground for athletes aspiring to compete at international levels.

questions.question: RK Narayan is the author of which pair of novels from the given alternatives?

options.text: 'The Cat and Shakespeare' and 'On the Ganga Ghat'
'The English Teacher' and 'Walking with the Mahatma'

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**'The English Teacher' and 'Walking with the Mahatma'**__.

__Key Points__

__
 
• **R.K. Narayan** is one of the most celebrated Indian authors writing in English, known for his work set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi.
 
• **'The English Teacher'** is part of the informal trilogy along with 'Swami and Friends' and 'The Bachelor of Arts,' focusing on the life of the protagonist Krishna.
 
• **'Walking with the Mahatma'** is another notable novel by Narayan, exploring themes of spirituality and the influence of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Both novels reflect Narayan's keen observation of Indian society and his ability to weave intricate tales with simplicity and humor.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **R.K. Narayan's Writing Style**

 
 
• Known for his simple and straightforward writing, Narayan's style is marked by a blend of humor, irony, and deep humanism.
 
• He draws heavily from Indian mythology and culture, making his work resonate deeply with Indian readers and those interested in Indian heritage.
 
• Narayan's works often depict the lives of ordinary people, highlighting their struggles and triumphs in a rapidly changing society.
 
 
 
• **Malgudi**
 
 
• Malgudi is a fictional town created by Narayan, serving as the setting for many of his novels and short stories.
 
• The town and its inhabitants are vividly described, making Malgudi almost a character in its own right within Narayan's works.
 
• Malgudi is symbolic of small-town India and provides a microcosm of Indian life.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Narayan was influenced by the ideas and philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi, which is reflected in his characters and themes.
 
• 'Walking with the Mahatma' delves into the impact of Gandhi's teachings on the protagonist's life and the broader Indian society.
 
 
 
• **Literary Contributions**
 
 
• R.K. Narayan's contributions to Indian English literature have been immense, earning him several prestigious awards including the Padma Bhushan and the Sahitya Akademi Award.
 
• His works have been translated into multiple languages, allowing a wider audience to appreciate his storytelling.

questions.question: Who built the Jaisalmer fort in 1156 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rawal Jaisal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jaisalmer Fort, also known as Sonar Quila or the Golden Fort, was built by **Rawal Jaisal** in 1156 AD.
 
• The fort is situated on Meru Hill in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is one of the largest fully preserved fortified cities in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the group "Hill Forts of Rajasthan".
 
• The fort is renowned for its massive yellow sandstone walls, which appear to change color with the setting sun.
 
• Rawal Jaisal was the founder of the city of Jaisalmer, and he established the fort as a strategic center for trade and defense.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architecture:**

 
 
• The fort's architecture includes intricate carvings, latticework, and jharokhas (overhanging enclosed balconies).
 
• It has three layers of walls: the outer layer (solid stone blocks), the middle layer (a mix of soft and hard stones), and the innermost layer (the main fort complex).
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The fort has witnessed several battles and has been an important trade route between India and Central Asia.
 
• It served as a strategic location for Rajput kings to defend against invasions.
 
 
 
• **Tourism:**
 
 
• Jaisalmer Fort is a major tourist attraction and houses several havelis (mansions), temples, and the Raj Mahal (Royal Palace).
 
• The fort's annual Desert Festival attracts numerous visitors, showcasing Rajasthani culture, music, and dance.
 
 
 
• **Current Status:**
 
 
• Despite its age, Jaisalmer Fort remains a functioning fort with a significant portion of the population still residing within its walls.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve and maintain the fort due to its historical and architectural significance.

questions.question: Which of the following states have witnessed effective implementation of land reform measures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kerala** implemented comprehensive land reforms in the 1960s and 1970s, focusing on the redistribution of land to the landless and ensuring security of tenure to tenants.
 
• **West Bengal** saw significant land reforms under the Left Front government in the late 1970s and 1980s, particularly through the Operation Barga initiative which recorded sharecroppers and gave them greater security of tenure.
 
• These reforms in Kerala and West Bengal led to an increase in agricultural productivity and a more equitable distribution of land.
 
• Both states have been recognized for reducing rural poverty and improving the socio-economic conditions of farmers through effective land reform measures.
 
• The success of land reforms in these states can be attributed to strong political will, effective implementation, and active participation of local communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Land Reforms**

 
 
• Land reforms involve the changing of laws, regulations, or customs regarding land ownership.
 
• They aim to redistribute land to benefit the landless, ensure fair distribution, and promote agricultural productivity and socio-economic development.
 
• Key components include land redistribution, tenancy reforms, and land consolidation.
 
 
 
• **Operation Barga**
 
 
• Launched in 1978 in West Bengal, Operation Barga aimed to record the names of sharecroppers (bargadars) to provide them with legal recognition and security of tenure.
 
• This initiative reduced the exploitation of sharecroppers by landlords and boosted agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Tenancy Reforms**
 
 
• These reforms aim to regulate the relationship between landlords and tenants, ensuring fair rents and security of tenure.
 
• They often involve the recording of tenants' rights and protection from eviction.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**
 
 
• Effective land reforms can lead to improved agricultural productivity and rural development.
 
• They can reduce rural poverty and income inequality, contributing to overall socio-economic progress.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement about lichens.

options.text: Lichens are seen slow-growing large coloured patches on the bark of trees.
Fungi are found in lichen living a symbiotic life.
Fungi and cyanobacteria both lives in lichens independently.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lichens are a symbiotic association between fungi and a photosynthetic partner, typically algae or cyanobacteria.
 
• The fungal component, known as the mycobiont, provides structure and protection while the photosynthetic partner, known as the photobiont, produces food through photosynthesis.
 
• Fungi and cyanobacteria do not live independently within lichens; they form a mutualistic relationship where both partners benefit.
 
• Lichens grow slowly and can form large, colored patches on surfaces like tree bark, rocks, and soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symbiosis**

 
 
• Symbiosis is an interaction between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.
 
• In lichens, the symbiotic relationship is between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lichens**
 
 
• Crustose: Crust-like lichens that adhere tightly to the substrate.
 
• Foliose: Leafy lichens that have a flat, leaf-like structure.

• Northern India experiences **warm days and cold nights during the summer season** due to the region's geographical and climatic conditions.
 
• The temperature difference between day and night is **significant in summer** due to clear skies and dry air.
 
• In summer, the **sun's intensity** leads to high daytime temperatures, but the heat dissipates quickly at night.
 
• The phenomenon is particularly noticeable in **desert regions** like Rajasthan, where the diurnal temperature variation is extreme.
 
• This pattern is a result of the **continental climate** experienced in Northern India, which lacks the moderating influence of large water bodies.

• **Diurnal Temperature Variation**

 
 
• It refers to the difference in temperature between the highest temperature during the day and the lowest temperature at night.
 
• This variation is more pronounced in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
 
 
• **Continental Climate**
 
 
• Characterized by significant seasonal temperature differences, with hot summers and cold winters.
 
• Influenced by the lack of nearby large water bodies which would otherwise moderate the temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Influence**
 
 
• Northern India’s topography, including the presence of the Thar Desert, contributes to the extreme temperature variations.
 
• The Himalayas also play a role in shaping the climate by blocking cold winds from Central Asia.

• Typically lasts from March to June, with peak temperatures in May and June.

questions.question: Who introduced the term 'triads' in the classification of elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Johann Dobereiner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Johann Dobereiner, a German chemist, introduced the concept of 'triads' in 1817.
 
• He observed that certain groups of three elements (triads) had similar chemical properties and that the atomic weight of the middle element was approximately the average of the other two.
 
• Dobereiner's Triads were an early attempt to classify elements based on their properties and paved the way for the development of the periodic table.
 
• Examples of Dobereiner's Triads include lithium, sodium, and potassium, as well as calcium, strontium, and barium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table Development:**

 
 
• The periodic table as we know it today was developed by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
 
• Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight and left gaps for elements that were yet to be discovered.
 
 
 
• **Law of Triads:**
 
 
• The Law of Triads states that the arithmetic mean of the atomic weights of the first and third elements in a triad is approximately equal to the atomic weight of the second element.
 
 
 
• **Other Early Classifications:**
 
 
• John Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves, which stated that every eighth element had similar properties.
 
• A.E.B. de Chancourtois introduced the telluric helix, a three-dimensional arrangement of the elements.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Law:**
 
 
• The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers, not atomic weights.
 
• This law was proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913 after he discovered the concept of atomic number.

questions.question: Identify a structure found in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mesosomes are invaginated structures found in prokaryotic cells, particularly in bacteria.
 
• They appear in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae within the bacterial cell.
 
• Mesosomes are involved in various cellular processes such as cell wall formation during cell division, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells.
 
• These structures are also associated with increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane for enzymatic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plastids**

 
 
• Plastids are double-membrane organelles found in the cells of plants and algae.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of food, most notably photosynthesis in chloroplasts.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, excluding the nucleus.
 
• It houses various organelles and is the site for most cellular processes.

• **Erythropoiesis:**

• **Anemia:**
 
 
• A condition in which there is a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin in the blood.

• **Blood Groups:**

questions.question: Which of the following is the best indicator of the borrowings of the Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue excluding borrowings.
 
• This deficit indicates the total amount of borrowing required by the government to meet its expenditure.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of a government's financial health and its reliance on borrowing to fund its activities.
 
• Fiscal deficit is usually expressed as a percentage of a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Monitoring the fiscal deficit helps in understanding the sustainability of a government's policies and its financial discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Deficit**

 
 
• Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit of a government excluding interest payments on past borrowings.
 
• It indicates the current fiscal condition and the borrowing needed to meet current expenses.
 
• Primary deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP) Deficit**
 
 
• BoP deficit occurs when a country's total imports of goods, services, and transfers exceed its total exports.
 
• It reflects the economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Deficit**
 
 
• Revenue deficit is the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
 
• It indicates that the government is not able to meet its current operational expenses from its revenue earnings.
 
 
 
• **Implications of High Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• A high fiscal deficit may lead to higher borrowing costs and increased public debt.
 
• It can also result in inflationary pressures if financed by printing more money.

__
 
• **Frogs have a three-chambered heart**, consisting of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• The three-chambered heart in amphibians like frogs allows for partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• This structure is efficient for their dual life in water and on land, where they can absorb oxygen through their skin.
 
• Unlike frogs, birds and mammals possess a more complex four-chambered heart, which completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heart Chambers in Vertebrates**

 
 
• **Fish:** Two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle)
 
• **Amphibians:** Three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle)
 
• **Reptiles:** Typically three-chambered heart, except for crocodiles which have four chambers
 
• **Birds and Mammals:** Four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles)
 
 
 
• **Functions of Heart Chambers**
 
 
• Atria receive blood from the body and lungs.
 
• Ventricles pump blood out to the body and lungs.
 
• A four-chambered heart allows for complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is more efficient for high-energy demands.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory Systems**
 
 
• **Single Circulatory System:** Found in fish, blood passes through the heart once during each complete circuit.
 
• **Double Circulatory System:** Found in amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals, blood passes through the heart twice, providing more efficient oxygenation.
 
 
 
• **Adaptive Significance**
 
 
• A four-chambered heart supports endothermy (warm-bloodedness) in birds and mammals.
 
• Efficient circulation is crucial for sustaining high metabolic rates and activity levels.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the State Executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney General of India**__.

__
 
• The State Executive comprises the Governor, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State.
 
• The Governor is the head of the state and is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor in the exercise of his functions.
 
• The Advocate General of the State is the highest law officer in the state and is appointed by the Governor.
 
• The Attorney General of India is a central government position and is not part of the State Executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, and respites or remissions of punishment.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister and Council of Ministers**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the government in the state.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Advocate General of the State**
 
 
• The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
 
• The Advocate General's duty is to advise the state government on legal matters.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General of India**
 
 
• The Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Attorney General is not part of the State Executive and primarily deals with legal matters at the national level.

questions.question: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayanand Saraswati in which of the following years?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Arya Samaj** was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
 
• The Arya Samaj was established on **10 April 1875**.
 
• Swami Dayanand Saraswati was a prominent Hindu religious leader and reformer.
 
• The primary aim of Arya Samaj was to promote values and practices based on the infallibility of the Vedas.
 
• Arya Samaj played a crucial role in the social and religious reform movements in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Born as Mool Shankar Tiwari on 12 February 1824, he was a Hindu religious scholar and the founder of Arya Samaj.
 
• He emphasized the Vedic ideal of Brahmacharya and opposed idol worship.
 
• His teachings inspired several future leaders and reformers, including Mahatma Gandhi.

• The organization promotes the idea of monotheism and rejects idol worship.
 
• It advocates for the equal status of all individuals irrespective of caste, creed, or gender.

questions.question: Who gave the expanding universe hypothesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Edwin Hubble**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Edwin Hubble was an American astronomer who played a crucial role in establishing the field of extragalactic astronomy.
 
• In 1929, Hubble discovered that galaxies are moving away from each other, indicating that the universe is expanding.
 
• His observations led to the formulation of Hubble's Law, which quantifies the relationship between a galaxy's distance and its recessional velocity.
 
• Hubble's work provided the first observational evidence supporting the Big Bang theory of the origin of the universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hubble's Law**

 
 
• Hubble's Law states that the recessional velocity of a galaxy is directly proportional to its distance from us.
 
• The law is often expressed as v = H₀d, where v is the galaxy's recessional velocity, H₀ is the Hubble constant, and d is the distance to the galaxy.
 
 
 
• **Redshift**
 
 
• Redshift refers to the phenomenon where the light from an object is shifted to longer wavelengths as it moves away from the observer.
 
• Hubble used redshift measurements to determine the velocities of galaxies.
 
 
 
• **Big Bang Theory**
 
 
• The Big Bang Theory is the leading explanation for the origin of the universe, suggesting that it began as a singularity approximately 13.8 billion years ago.
 
• Hubble's discovery of the expanding universe provided significant support for this theory.
 
 
 
• **Cosmology**
 
 
• Cosmology is the scientific study of the large-scale properties and evolution of the universe.
 
• Hubble's work laid the foundation for modern cosmology, influencing subsequent research and theories.

questions.question: Who among the following is the Padma Shri 2022 awardee Kuchipudi dancer credited with reviving the Kakatiyam dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padmaja Reddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padmaja Reddy is a renowned Kuchipudi dancer who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• She is credited with reviving the ancient Kakatiyam dance form, bringing it back into the cultural mainstream.
 
• Her efforts have been instrumental in preserving and promoting this traditional dance form, which was almost forgotten.
 
• Padmaja Reddy has performed extensively both in India and abroad, showcasing the rich heritage of Kuchipudi and Kakatiyam dance.
 
• Her dedication to dance and her innovative choreography have earned her numerous accolades and recognition in the field of performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms originating from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its fast rhythms, fluid movements, and vibrant expressions.
 
• The dance form integrates elements of dance, music, and acting, often telling stories from Indian epics and mythology.
 
• Kuchipudi performances typically include a combination of pure dance (nritta), expressive dance (nritya), and dramatic storytelling (natya).
 
 
 
• **Kakatiyam Dance Form**
 
 
• The Kakatiyam dance form has its roots in the Kakatiya dynasty, which ruled parts of South India in the 12th and 13th centuries.
 
• It is characterized by its unique movements and postures, which are different from mainstream classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form was largely forgotten over the centuries and has been revived thanks to the efforts of dedicated dancers like Padmaja Reddy.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded to individuals for their distinguished contributions in various fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• Instituted in 1954, the award recognizes exceptional and distinguished service in any field.
 
• Recipients of the Padma Shri are announced annually on Republic Day.

questions.question: Which of the following sites would be suitable for observing the architecture of the Harappan civilisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banawali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Banawali is an archaeological site located in the Fatehabad district of Haryana, India.
 
• It is one of the significant sites of the Harappan civilisation, often associated with the mature phase of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The site exhibits the typical features of Harappan urban planning, including well-planned streets, drainage systems, and fortified structures.
 
• Artifacts such as pottery, seals, and tools found at Banawali provide insight into the daily life and trade practices of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• Also known as Harappan Civilization, it flourished around 2500-1900 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, Lothal, and Rakhigarhi.
 
• It is known for its advanced urban infrastructure, including grid-planned cities, sophisticated drainage systems, and large non-residential buildings.
 
 
 
• **Artifacts:**
 
 
• Artifacts such as terracotta figurines, pottery, tools, and seals have been crucial in understanding the Harappan way of life.
 
• Seals often depicted animals and script, suggesting a form of communication and administrative control.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning:**
 
 
• Harappan cities were known for their advanced urban planning, with streets laid out in a grid pattern and sophisticated drainage systems.
 
• Public buildings, granaries, and baths indicate a high level of social organization.
 
 
 
• **Trade:**
 
 
• The Harappans engaged in extensive trade, both within the civilization and with neighboring regions such as Mesopotamia.
 
• Evidence of trade includes the discovery of Harappan seals and goods in distant lands.

questions.question: Kanchenjunga' and 'K2' are names of__________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mountain peaks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanchenjunga** is the third highest mountain peak in the world, with an elevation of 8,586 meters (28,169 feet).
 
• **K2**, also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, is the second highest mountain peak in the world, standing at 8,611 meters (28,251 feet).
 
• Both peaks are part of the **Himalayan and Karakoram ranges** respectively, which are renowned for their high-altitude mountains.
 
• Kanchenjunga is located on the border between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim, while K2 is located on the border between Pakistan and China.
 
• These peaks are popular destinations for mountaineers and adventurers from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayan Range:**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The range has some of the planet's highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga.
 
• The Himalayas span five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Karakoram Range:**
 
 
• The Karakoram is a large mountain range spanning the borders between Pakistan, India, and China, with the northwest extremity of the range extending to Afghanistan and Tajikistan.
 
• K2 is the highest point in the Karakoram range.
 
• The Karakoram is home to some of the world's largest glaciers, such as the Siachen Glacier.
 
 
 
• **Mountaineering:**
 
 
• Mountaineering is the sport of climbing mountains, which involves skills such as rock climbing, ice climbing, and navigating through various terrains.
 
• The activity is often pursued for recreation, adventure, and achieving personal goals.
 
• Mountaineering requires proper equipment, training, and acclimatization to high altitudes to ensure safety.
